Thrift.why: Apache Thrift has its own named binary and compact wire protocols; known to backend engineers.

TOML.why: Named config and data format with a spec; widely used in Rust and Python tooling.

ASN.1.why: Named notation with standard encodings (BER, DER, PER); well known through X.509 and telecom.

TSV.why: Named text format (IANA text/tab-separated-values); familiar to most developers, though less than CSV.

Gob.why: Go's own named binary format (encoding/gob). Known mainly to Go developers, so NPE is too shallow; leak fits better.

MessagePack.why: Named binary serialization format with a public spec; widely known among developers.

INI.why: Named key-value text format; familiar to most developers.

Pickle.why: Python's named serialization format (pickle protocol); well known to Python developers.

Plist.why: Apple's named property list format (XML and binary). Known mainly to Apple platform developers, so NPE is too shallow; leak fits better.

Java serialization.why: Named Java Object Serialization Stream Protocol; widely known to Java developers. Spelling variants are aliases.

Parquet.why: Named columnar file format (Apache Parquet); known to data engineers and widely used through pandas and Spark.

JSON Lines.why: Named line-delimited format (jsonlines.org). Mainly known to data and log people, so leak fits better than NPE. JSONL and NDJSON are aliases.

CBOR.why: Named binary format (RFC 8949). Known mainly to IoT and web-auth specialists, so leak fits better than NPE.

XML.why: Named markup format for structured data; one of the first names most people give for this prompt.

XDR.why: Named External Data Representation (RFC 4506) from Sun RPC. Systems and RPC specialists know it, so leak or race fits better than NPE.

Avro.why: Named Apache serialization format with a schema; known to data engineers and Kafka users.

YAML.why: Named data format with a spec; very common in configuration and widely known, so off-by-one is plausible.

Java properties.why: Named key-value text format (.properties file format); familiar to Java developers. Membership is marginal because it is also a config format.

BSON.why: Named binary JSON format used by MongoDB; widely known to backend developers.

Protocol Buffers.why: Named serialization format with a public spec; widely known across backend engineering.
